fields.h1: Build a Beta Feedback Survey Before Launch Day
fields.hero_description: Build a beta feedback survey that records the build behind every answer and saves results to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Every Answer Tied to a Build and a Tester
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the beta feedback survey, the rules that act on its answers, and the database that keeps every round.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for your beta

Describe the product, the testers, and what this round has to settle. Emergent drafts the questions, and a follow-up prompt adds or cuts one before the next build goes out.
fields.feature_2:
Each answer filed under its build

Every response is a row in a database you own, saved with the tester, the build number, and the device. Put build 2.3 beside build 2.4 without merging two spreadsheets.
fields.feature_3:
An alert when a crash repeats

Set the line, such as 8 crash reports on one build. The app then posts the build number and the testers' steps to a Slack channel, or emails the engineer who owns the fix.
fields.feature_4:
One question per screen on a phone

Testers answer one question per screen on a phone, with the test device still in hand. Emergent puts no cap on how many testers answer, in an open beta or a closed beta.
fields.feature_5:
Crash reports sent to your tracker

Connect the issue tracker your team works in through its API. The app files each crash report there with the build number and the tester's steps, ready for the next triage.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. Reuse the same survey for the next beta, with every earlier round of answers still sitting in your database.

fields.usecase_heading: What Four Betas Caught Before Launch
fields.tab_content_1:
11 barcode crashes, all on build 2.4

Copperwick ships a weekly build of its meal-planning app to 60 beta testers, each build with a 4-question check-in. When 8 or more testers report the same crash on one build, the app posts to #beta-bugs in Slack. On build 2.4, 11 of 47 testers said it crashed while scanning a barcode, and the post carried their steps.
fields.tab_content_2:
Swaps score 80 from managers, 71 from staff

Lanternby ran shift swaps as a 3-week beta, then closed it with the 10-statement System Usability Scale. Of 42 testers, 36 answered, for an average of 74. The 12 managers scored it 80 and the 24 staff 71. Staff send the swap requests, and the team rewrote the request screen before launch.
fields.tab_content_3:
All 9 offline thermostats run firmware 1.2

Ormsley put 40 beta thermostats in homes. Each Friday, households answer a 3-question check-in on a phone, one question per screen, starting with whether the thermostat went offline. In week 3, 38 answered and 9 said yes. All 9 ran firmware 1.2, and the app emailed firmware engineer Saffi Brennick the list.
fields.tab_content_4:
7 teams want scheduled reports before launch

Velloway closed its analytics dashboard beta with an exit survey to 25 design-partner teams. Asked whether they would keep using it after launch, 18 of 25 said yes. Asked what would stop a rollout, 7 teams named scheduled reports, more than any other answer. Launch moved 2 weeks to add them.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Beta Feedback Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to run a beta feedback survey that turns tester answers into fixes before launch, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what this beta has to settle
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Record the build with every answer
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask for the steps behind each crash
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the 2 or 3 decisions the beta feeds, such as whether a build is stable enough to ship or whether a new screen makes sense. Each question should serve one of them. Cut the rest before a tester ever sees the survey.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask testers for nothing they would have to look up. Give the device a short pick list, and save the build number with each answer. A crash report helps only when it points to one build, and a trend needs two builds side by side.
fields.howto_step_3_des: During the beta, send a short check-in with each build: rate this build, did it crash, what were you doing, and what confused you. Save the longer questions for the end, after testers have used every part of the product.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask what the tester tapped right before the crash, which gives an engineer a report to repeat. An open question about issues gets answers like it's buggy. Give the steps question its own screen, and show it only to testers who said the app crashed.
fields.howto_step_5_des: At the end of a round, ask the same 10 usability statements every time, so this beta's score compares with the last one. Split the score by role or plan, because one group can pull an average down while another holds it up.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set the alert line before the first build
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide what counts as a pattern, such as 8 testers naming one crash on a single build, and who hears about it. Put the line and the Slack channel or email address in your prompt, and the app sends the alert when a build crosses it.
fields.howto_step_7_des: On the last day, ask each tester whether they would keep using the product after launch and what would stop them. Count the blockers, fix the top one first, and tell testers what changed before you invite them to the next beta.

faq_plan.q: What is a beta feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: A beta feedback survey is the questionnaire beta testers answer about a product before its public release: what broke, what confused them, and what would make them stay. In software development, a beta test is the second phase of software testing, and the survey is how testers report back from it.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a beta feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe the beta in Emergent's AI survey builder: the product, who is testing it, how often builds ship, and the decisions the answers feed. Emergent builds the survey, its logic, and the database behind it. Between builds, change any question with a follow-up prompt.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a beta feedback survey ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask questions that end in a fix or a launch call. Beyond a stability rating and a crash report, ask which feature they used this week, what they expected a screen to do, and what they had to work around. On the last day, ask whether they plan to stay once the product launches.

faq_plan.q: When should a beta feedback survey use a yes or no question instead of a rating?
faq_plan.a: Use yes or no when the answer should trigger something: did the app crash, did setup finish, did you open the new screen this week. A yes can open a follow-up for the steps, and the counts compare cleanly across builds. Use a rating for anything with degrees, and see the yes no questions survey for the format at full length.

faq_plan.q: How often should you send a beta feedback survey during a beta?
faq_plan.a: Survey testers once per build, or weekly if builds ship more often, plus one longer survey on the last day. Keep each check-in to about 2 minutes: short enough to answer right after using the build. Emergent can add a reminder too: the app emails testers who have not answered that build's check-in.

faq_plan.q: What is a good usability score in a beta feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: Anything above 68 on the System Usability Scale. MeasuringU reports that the average SUS score from all 500 studies is a 68, and a score above it counts as above average. The scale is a 10 item questionnaire with 5 response options, and scores run from 0 to 100 without being percentages. Compare each beta with your own last round as well.

faq_plan.q: How should beta feedback survey questions change once customers start paying?
faq_plan.a: Shift from what broke to why people stay. Beta questions tie each answer to a build; after launch, ask why they bought, how setup went, and what nearly stopped them, which is the job of a post purchase survey. Keep one stability question to line post-launch answers up with the beta.

faq_plan.q: How do you get beta testers to finish a beta feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: Keep it short, send it right after they use the build, and tell them what changed because of the last round. A tester who sees a reported crash fixed in the next build has a reason to answer again. Emergent can build the survey as one question per screen, which suits testers answering on the phone they are testing.

faq_plan.q: Should a beta feedback survey differ for a closed beta and an open beta?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A closed beta test involves a limited number of people who evaluate the application. With that few, ask for detailed steps and follow up with each tester by name. In an open beta, a large number of testers put the product through its paces: keep the survey short and read the answers as counts.

faq_plan.q: Can a beta feedback survey include a fun question?
faq_plan.a: Yes, one, placed last. Ask testers to describe the build in 3 words, or to name the feature they would miss most if it disappeared. It gives a tired tester an easy final answer. Keep jokes out of the crash and usability questions, and borrow from funny survey questions only for that closing slot.

plan.angle: Searchers want a beta feedback survey they can send to testers, not a glossary entry. This page is the survey itself across four beta programs, each ending in a release decision: a short check-in after every mobile build with a crash alert, an end-of-beta usability score split by role, a weekly phone check-in for a hardware field test that emails the firmware engineer, and an exit survey that ranks launch blockers. The FAQ covers which questions to ask, yes or no versus rating, how often to survey, what a usability score means, closed versus open betas and how the questions change after launch. Paying-customer surveys belong to the post purchase survey sibling; app-wide feedback belongs to the app feedback survey sibling.

Lanternby closes a 3-week beta of shift swaps in its scheduling software with the 10-statement usability questionnaire; 36 testers answer and average 74, with 12 managers at 80 and 24 staff at 71, so the team rewrites the swap request screen staff use.

Ormsley ships 40 beta thermostats and asks each household one question per screen every Friday on a phone; in week 3, 38 answer, 9 say the thermostat went offline, all 9 run firmware 1.2, and the app emails firmware engineer Saffi Brennick.

Velloway closes the beta of its analytics dashboard with an exit survey to 25 design-partner teams; 18 of 25 would keep using it after launch, 7 name single sign-on as the blocker, and launch moves 2 weeks to add it.
